Verify fact reachability:state:MethaneState:line:12 = refuted. Source: MethaneState at line 8 in Region1; no PumpControl-level initial edge to it in source either.
issues.expected: PumpControl's initial entry must include an edge to MethaneState as an alternative initial target.
issues.observed: No [*] -> MethaneState edge exists in PumpControl scope in the complete FCSTM transition inventory. MethaneState is reachable only via event-triggered transition from PumpState (transition:line:15 on _Methane_Flow_Detected), but that path is itself unreachable from the top-level initial.
issues.reason: The contract as extracted specifies property=initial_entry with owner=PumpControl and target=MethaneState. The complete FCSTM transition inventory contains no such edge. This is an exact negative inventory result evaluated against the contract's stated property.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL text 'the system can transition to the MethaneState substate' more naturally describes an event-triggered reachability claim than an initial-entry requirement. The model does provide a PumpState -> MethaneState transition on _Methane_Flow_Detected. In a concurrent-region model, multiple initial alternatives from the composite are structurally inexpressible. The contract may be a misclassification of a reachability obligation.
issues.title: No PumpControl-level initial entry edge to MethaneState exists

issues.basis: Contract REF-011 (NL5, state=MethaneState, action='pump controlling or monitoring methane flow', no phase hint). Reference inspection facts: actions count = 0. FCSTM MethaneState declaration at line 12 has no action fields.
issues.expected: MethaneState must carry an action representing pump controlling or monitoring methane flow as its ongoing state behavior.
issues.observed: The FCSTM model contains zero actions across all states. MethaneState (state:MethaneState:line:12) has no entry, do, or exit action defined.
issues.reason: The contract requires a state_action in MethaneState. The model has no actions anywhere. The binding hints provide state and action but no lifecycle phase, so S4 is not applicable; the precise claim remains a W1 candidate with predicate_id=null.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL phrase 'indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow' could be read as a semantic description of the state's purpose rather than a formal action obligation. The binding hints do not specify a lifecycle phase, so S4 cannot be applied. If the NL intended only to describe what the state means rather than mandate a do-action, no violation exists.
issues.title: MethaneState lacks the required methane flow monitoring action

issues.basis: Contract REF-013 (segment NL5, source=WaterState, target=MethaneState). FCSTM complete transition list: 10 edges, none from WaterState to MethaneState. Source inventory: tr_0004 is PumpState -> MethaneState (not WaterState -> MethaneState). Region1 transitions in FCSTM: line 13 (initial), 14, 15, 16, 17.
issues.expected: A transition from WaterState to MethaneState must exist within Region1, enabling sequential progression through all three operating substates.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory (10 edges) contains no WaterState -> MethaneState edge. The available transitions from WaterState are only WaterState -> PumpState (transition:line:16 on _Water_Flow_Completed). The transition to MethaneState exists only from PumpState (transition:line:15 on _Methane_Flow_Detected), not from WaterState.
issues.reason: The derived contract REF-013 requires a WaterState -> MethaneState transition. The complete closed transition inventory contains no such edge. Both endpoint states exist and are exactly bound. This is an exact negative inventory result per the complete-inventory absence protocol.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL text 'the system can transition to the MethaneState substate' does not explicitly specify WaterState as the source; it says 'the system' can transition to MethaneState. The contract extraction derived WaterState as source based on sequential ordering (NL3 PumpState -> NL4 WaterState -> NL5 MethaneState), but the NL could equally describe PumpState -> MethaneState (which exists in the model on _Methane_Flow_Detected). The source inventory confirms the author drew PumpState -> MethaneState, not WaterState -> MethaneState.
issues.title: No WaterState to MethaneState transition exists in the closed model

issues.basis: NL3, FCSTM transition:line:27 (PumpControl scope, [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial), FCSTM transition:line:13 (Region1 scope, [*] -> PumpState), verify_facts refuted reachability for state:PumpState:line:10, inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_state_refs containing only root/PumpControl/UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.expected: Within PumpControl scope, the initial pseudostate edge must target PumpState as the first/default entry.
issues.observed: The only PumpControl-scoped initial edge is [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:27), a compiler-synthetic placeholder. The [*] -> PumpState edge exists in Region1 scope (transition:line:13) but cannot satisfy the PumpControl-owned initial entry contract. PumpState is unreachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The NL explicitly requires PumpControl's first entry to be PumpState. The FCSTM's PumpControl-scoped initial edge targets UnspecifiedInitial instead. The Region1-scoped edge is a different owner and cannot discharge this obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The Region1-scoped initial edge [*] -> PumpState (transition:line:13) does enter PumpState when Region1 is activated. However, Region1 itself is never entered because PumpControl's owner-local initial edge goes to UnspecifiedInitial, not to Region1 or any of its children. The scoped owner rule requires the initial edge to be owned by PumpControl, not by a nested region.
issues.title: PumpControl initial entry to PumpState is absent; owner-local edge targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial

issues.basis: NL4, FCSTM transition:line:27 (PumpControl scope initial edge), verify_facts refuted reachability for state:WaterState:line:11, source inventory showing no PumpControl->WaterState initial transition.
issues.expected: Within PumpControl scope, an initial entry edge must target WaterState as an alternative first entry.
issues.observed: No PumpControl-scoped initial edge targets WaterState. The only PumpControl-scoped initial edge is [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:27). WaterState is unreachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The NL describes WaterState as an alternative initial substate of PumpControl. The FCSTM has no PumpControl-scoped initial edge to WaterState. The operational transition from PumpState to WaterState satisfies a different property (transition_endpoints, covered by REF-012) but not the initial_entry obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: The system can also transition to the WaterState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the water flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: WaterState is reachable from PumpState via the _Water_Flow_Detected transition (transition:line:14) once the system enters Region1. However, the NL requires WaterState as an initial entry alternative of PumpControl, not merely as a reachable descendant. The initial entry obligation is distinct from operational reachability within the state.
issues.title: PumpControl initial entry to WaterState as alternative is absent
